name: MOT with similar-looking objects where motion wins, plus training-free weak motion cues as no-fly controls (DanceTrack CVPR 2022, SportsMOT/MixSort ICCV 2023, DiffMOT CVPR 2024, TOPICTrack TIP 2025, DeconfuseTrack CVPR 2024)

Independence note: DanceTrack and DiffMOT both report the same DanceTrack-val IoU baseline (HOTA 44.7, AssA 25.3, IDF1 36.8) and both rely on the YOLOX/ByteTrack detection protocol - DiffMOT's motion-model table reuses DanceTrack's setting, so they are not independent confirmations of 'learned motion beats Kalman'. OC-SORT and Hybrid-SORT (velocity direction / weak cues) were reviewed earlier (research_flyvis_advantage_readout_2026-10-25) and are not repeated.
full_text_checked: DanceTrack: full arXiv v3 PDF downloaded; section 4.2 Oracle Analysis, Table 2 and Figure 4 caption read as extracted text (check-mark columns lost in extraction, row-to-cue mapping reconstructed from the number of check marks and the authors' text), Tables 4-5 read via arXiv HTML. SportsMOT/MixSort: arXiv HTML v2 read (dataset section, MixSort method, Tables 3-6); Table 6 layout came out garbled in extraction. DiffMOT: arXiv HTML v2 read (method, Table 5 motion-model ablation, Tables 1-3). TOPIC: arXiv HTML v2 read in two parts (method incl. motion-level definition, Table II, test tables V-VII, BEE24 description); Figure 9 (alpha sensitivity) is an image, its curve values were NOT accessible. DeconfuseTrack: arXiv HTML read (DDA modules, Table 3 ablation); the arXiv PDF was too large to fetch; the CVF supplementary PDF was not opened. No code repository of any of the five was opened.
inputs_state_output: Authors' setups. DanceTrack oracle (Table 2): GT boxes, three association cues compared - IoU of adjacent-frame boxes, linear Kalman motion, pretrained ReID appearance; output = identity assignment; no learned fusion. SportsMOT/MixSort: strong base = IoU/Kalman motion association of ByteTrack or OC-SORT; added branch = a MixFormer-like template-search appearance model (4 mixed-attention layers, heatmap head predicting the template centre), per track the Kalman prediction defines a search crop, each detection whose centre lies inside the crop gets its heatmap response as visual similarity V (0 otherwise); fusion point = cost matrix before Hungarian; state = track template + Kalman state. Note: in SportsMOT the BASE is motion and the added branch is appearance - the reverse of our case. DiffMOT: base = IoU + ReID (Deep OC-SORT style dynamic appearance and adaptive weighting) in stage 1, IoU only in stage 2; replaced node = motion predictor (D2MP diffusion, HMINet conditioned on the last n=5 box/delta frames) instead of the Kalman filter; output = predicted box for IoU. TOPIC: two parallel matchings per frame - motion (IoU to prediction) and appearance (FastReID AGW, 384x384, plus an Attention-based Appearance Reconstruction Module AARM); a per-tracklet scalar 'motion level' = 1 - IoU(box at last observation t-k, box at t) in [0,1] (new tracklets start at 1) selects which matching result is accepted: motion level >= alpha -> appearance match, else motion match (alpha=0 appearance-only, alpha=1 motion-only); conflicts between the two rounds are resolved by a second round. DeconfuseTrack: base = ByteTrack (Kalman IoU) with an external SBS-50 FastReID appearance model; Decomposed Data Association splits association into sub-problems (DDM, TDM, ADM) using non-learned rules; appearance cosine is consulted only where positional cues are ambiguous (confusion reduction factor kappa = 0.3); Occlusion-aware NMS keeps more occluded detections. Ours: strong base = frozen MASA-R50 RoIAlign appearance cosines (exemplar snapped to a detection, previous target, bank, 32 PCA products) per real detection region; added branch = FlyVis activity from a bounded grey eye crop (34 output types incl. T4/T5 plus 6-neighbour means) with temporal state over exemplar+search frames; fusion = concatenation into one gradient boosting (identity stage), then a full-box transfer gate before ByteTrack matching. Key structural difference: in all five sources the motion cue is a box-trajectory cue (IoU to prediction, Kalman/learned box predictor, motion level from box overlap), not a pixel-level motion-energy map like T4/T5; none feeds motion features into a per-region identity classifier.
fusion_and_training: DanceTrack oracle: no fusion training, simple combinations of cost cues. MixSort: late score fusion M = alpha*IoU + (1-alpha)*V solved by Hungarian; alpha is a hand-set scalar swept on SportsMOT test (Table 4); the MixFormer appearance branch is trained separately on SportsMOT (training details not read); the motion base has no parameters except Kalman. DiffMOT: the motion predictor is trained alone (smooth L1 on box deltas, Adam 1e-4, 800 epochs, batch 2048); appearance fusion inherited from Deep OC-SORT (adaptive weighting) - no joint training. TOPIC: hard gating by a training-free scalar (motion level vs threshold alpha), no learned fusion; only the ReID model is trained (FastReID AGW, Adam, 120 epochs, lr 3.5e-4). DeconfuseTrack: rule-based decomposition, no learnable components in DDA; appearance used only when motion is insufficient 'to limit interference with motion' - this is an explicit device that prevents the weaker/unreliable cue from damaging the base. Nothing is zero-initialised or residually fused; the protection of the base is achieved by (a) hand-set weight alpha (MixSort), (b) gating by a reliability scalar (TOPIC motion level, DeconfuseTrack ambiguity rules). None of the sources trains a weak branch jointly over a strong frozen base, so they say nothing about modality imbalance in joint training.
labels_and_loss: DanceTrack/ DeconfuseTrack/ TOPIC fusion: no labels for fusion - association rules are training-free; ReID models (pretrained ReID in DanceTrack; FastReID SBS-50 on MOT17+MOT20 in DeconfuseTrack; FastReID AGW in TOPIC) use standard identity classification/triplet training [uncertain: ReID loss details not read]. MixSort: the MixFormer-like appearance model is trained to predict the template centre heatmap in the search region (a single-object-tracking style label) [uncertain: loss form not read]. DiffMOT: regression of box deltas (smooth L1), no identity label at all. No source mines hard negatives of similar neighbours for the fusion stage; DanceTrack only visualises with t-SNE (Figure 4) that ReID features of different dancers are 'highly entangled' while MOT17 features are separable. Class imbalance is not discussed.
data_camera_resolution_rate: DanceTrack: 100 videos (40 train / 25 val / 35 test, test labels private), 105,855 frames, 5,292 s, 20 FPS (Table 1), mostly static camera, indoor/outdoor dance stages, uniform appearance by design; resolution not stated in the text read [uncertain: commonly 1280x720 or higher]. SportsMOT: 240 sequences (45 train / 45 val / 150 test), 150,379 frames, 1,629,490 boxes, 25 FPS, 720P, basketball/volleyball/football broadcast overhead shots with camera motion (panning) [uncertain: degree of camera motion]. DiffMOT: DanceTrack, SportsMOT, MOT17, MOT20 (appendix). TOPIC: MOT17, MOT20, TAO, DanceTrack, GMOT-40, BEE24 (36 videos, 25 FPS, 950x590, five beehive setups, small similar-looking bees). DeconfuseTrack: MOT17 and MOT20 only; camera motion mentioned, no compensation. BDD100K-like data: NONE of the five sources uses BDD100K, KITTI or any driving data; none reports low light or glare subsets. DanceTrack and BEE24 isolate the 'same look' regime; SportsMOT adds fast non-linear motion; MOT17/MOT20 are pedestrian crowds.

distinguishing_ablations: Directly relevant pattern across sources: the gain of an added cue depends on which cue is the base and on the ambiguity regime. (a) Appearance over motion when objects look alike: DanceTrack Table 4 DeepSORT vs SORT -2.0 HOTA; oracle Table 2 adding appearance to IoU+Kalman drops 69.4 -> 59.7 HOTA - the added branch DAMAGES the base when it carries entangled identity information and is fused with a fixed weight. (b) SportsMOT alpha sweep shows the same branch can be mildly useful (+0.3..+1.3 HOTA) only at a tuned weight and is catastrophic alone; the optimum differs per sport (0.8/0.5/0.4), i.e. per regime. (c) TOPIC is the only source with a 'serial vs gated' contrast: naive serial appearance ~+0.1..+0.4 HOTA, gating by a training-free motion-level scalar +1.3..+2.0 HOTA over ByteTrack - the gain comes from WHEN each cue is trusted, not from a new feature. (d) DeconfuseTrack: the purely motion module DDM gives +0.1 HOTA over ByteTrack (essentially nothing); the appearance-assisted modules give +0.5..+0.7; over an appearance-heavy base (DeepSORT) IDF1 slightly falls - analogous to our observation that a second cue adds little over a strong appearance base. (e) DiffMOT replaces only the motion predictor: Kalman -> D2MP +8.9 HOTA on DanceTrack val with IoU-only association (note the table's Kalman row 46.8 vs DanceTrack's 47.8 for the same nominal setting). No source contains an equal-capacity non-informative branch control, permuted features, or seeds/variance; none reports confidence intervals; all are single runs. No source measures adding a weak MOTION branch over a STRONG APPEARANCE base in a regime where appearance is strong (our case); the closest is DeconfuseTrack's DDM (+0.1 HOTA) and TOPIC's gating.
explanations_addressed: (1) Fly carries no unique identity information beyond appearance: design analogy/caution - DanceTrack and DeconfuseTrack show that in pedestrian-like data (MOT17) box motion and appearance are largely redundant (oracle IoU-only 98.1 HOTA; DDM +0.1); a motion cue adds information mainly when appearance is entangled (DanceTrack, BEE24). For BDD100K cars/pedestrians with MASA cosines 0.955 vs 0.103 the appearance regime is closer to MOT17 than to DanceTrack - consistent with explanation (1). Not direct evidence for FlyVis features. (2) Information exists but fusion ignores it (modality imbalance): not addressed for training (no joint training anywhere); indirectly addressed for fixed fusion - TOPIC shows that a gate by a reliability scalar extracts gains that serial/additive fusion misses; this argues for testing a regime-gated fusion before claiming 'no information'. (3) Saved readout features lost the information: not addressed. (4) FlyVis lacks a lobula/identity pathway: not addressed; the sources use box-level motion, not neural motion maps. (5) Motion helps only in subsets diluted by averaging: DIRECT design evidence - per-sport optimal alpha (SportsMOT Table 4), TOPIC motion-level gating and per-dataset conflict rates (15.4% GMOT-40, 13.3% DanceTrack), DeconfuseTrack's 'appearance only when motion is ambiguous'; all imply that the benefit of the secondary cue concentrates in ambiguity subsets. Our analysis should stratify by a training-free ambiguity/motion-level scalar. (6) Ceiling too low (+2.8 pp perfect identity vs +2 pp threshold): caution - in these sources the whole effect of the secondary cue or gating is +0.1..+2.0 HOTA, i.e. small relative to totals; does not inform our utility ceiling directly.
evidence_strength: All five are peer-reviewed (CVPR 2022, ICCV 2023, CVPR 2024 x2, TIP 2025) [uncertain: venues of DanceTrack, SportsMOT, DiffMOT from memory]; public code/data reported (DanceTrack, MixSort, TOPICTrack repos) but not verified. Single runs, no variance, no CIs, no equal-capacity controls; ablations partly on test sets (SportsMOT alpha sweep on test). DanceTrack/DiffMOT share protocol (not independent). Overall: moderate for the qualitative claim 'motion wins over appearance when objects look alike, and a secondary cue helps only when gated/weighted by regime'; weak for any quantitative transfer, and not evidence for BDD100K (no driving data).
difference_from_tried: We already tried: T4/T5 motion consistency features, neighbour-relative features, tagged previous target, bank, and gradient boosting over concatenated MASA + fly features (boosting can in principle learn regime splits). What is new from these sources: (a) an explicit training-free regime scalar (TOPIC motion level = 1 - IoU(last observed box, predicted/current box); DeconfuseTrack ambiguity = closeness of top-2 positional costs) used as a HARD gate deciding which cue is trusted per track, rather than letting the boosting discover it; (b) box-trajectory motion cues (Kalman/velocity-direction/learned box predictor) as the no-fly equivalent of the fly's motion contribution; (c) the reverse-role lesson: in DanceTrack the strong branch is motion, and appearance damages it - we have never measured whether OUR fly branch damages MASA in a subset (only mean increments). If our boosting already received geometry and motion-consistency features (it did: geometry AUC 0.92-0.93), mechanism (b) is largely already present; mechanism (a) is only partly new because boosting can split on geometry - the difference is evaluation by stratum and a prespecified gate, not a new feature.
math_precheck: CPU, saved features only (train26 and fit104 feature files of the hybrid identity runs, e.g. runs/z13_hybrid_fly_confirm_20261026/train26_features_{D,C,R1}.npz, and the fit104 features of runs/z13_hybrid_identity_v2_20261026). Step 1 (regime scalar, no training): for each query compute (i) TOPIC-style motion level m = 1 - IoU(track's last observed box, tracker prediction) and (ii) an appearance-ambiguity margin a = MASA cosine(top-1 candidate) - cosine(top-2 candidate) to the exemplar, plus (iii) a neighbour-crowding count (other detections with IoU>0 to the eye crop). Step 2 (where appearance fails): with out-of-fold appearance-only predictions, compute the identity error rate and the perfect-identity utility ceiling share inside strata of m (tertiles) and a (low margin < 0.1 vs rest). If >= 70% of the +2.8 pp ceiling is concentrated in a stratum covering <= 20% of queries, gated fusion is worth testing; if appearance errors are spread uniformly, the 'diluted subset' explanation is rejected. Step 3 (complementarity inside the stratum): fraction of appearance-wrong queries in the ambiguous stratum where the FlyVis-only (D) top-1 is right, versus the same fraction for a no-fly box-motion score (Kalman/velocity-direction consistency: cosine between track velocity and candidate displacement, plus normalised centre distance to prediction) and for eye input R1. Step 4 (oracle-gated upper bound): utility of a combination that uses fly-assisted boosting only inside the stratum and appearance-only outside, with the gate threshold chosen on calibration videos (fit104) and evaluated once on train26, paired video bootstrap; compare to the same gate with the box-motion score and with R1 in place of fly. Decision rule: STOP the FlyVis gated-fusion line if (a) in the ambiguous stratum the fly-right/appearance-wrong fraction is not larger than that of the no-fly box-motion score by a CI-separated margin, or (b) the gated combination's train26 utility gain over appearance-only has an upper CI bound below the share of the +2 pp criterion still missing (i.e. it cannot reach +2 pp even at its upper bound), or (c) the gated fly version is not better than the gated box-motion or R1 version (fly+X not > X). Proceed to any GPU work only if fly beats box-motion and R1 inside the stratum with a positive lower CI bound.
cue_role_and_regime: In the sources motion enters as (i) the primary association cost (IoU to Kalman/learned prediction - DanceTrack, DiffMOT, base of MixSort/DeconfuseTrack), (ii) a training-free gate/selector (TOPIC motion level decides appearance vs motion per tracklet; DeconfuseTrack positional ambiguity decides when to consult appearance), (iii) a fixed fusion weight (MixSort alpha). Targeted regimes: same class and same look (DanceTrack dancers, BEE24 bees, SportsMOT same-team uniforms), fast non-linear motion and crossing paths (DanceTrack, SportsMOT), crowd occlusion (MOT20, ONMS in DeconfuseTrack). Darkness and glare are NOT addressed by any source. For our bench, the role transferable to FlyVis is (ii) a per-candidate/per-track gate deciding when fly evidence is consulted, with regimes defined by a training-free scalar (motion level, appearance margin, crowding) - a gain on dancers or bees says nothing about BDD100K cars at night.
no_fly_equivalent_control: Cheapest controls of identical role: (1) Kalman/ByteTrack prediction IoU and normalised centre distance of each candidate to the prediction (already available in the tracker state); (2) OC-SORT style velocity-direction consistency: cosine between the track's last-k velocity and the vector from last observation to candidate centre (training-free, ~2 numbers per candidate); (3) TOPIC motion level as the same gate scalar but with the box-motion score in place of FlyVis; (4) eye input R1 (raw grey crop statistics, same features shape) and stock FlyVis C; (5) a small MLP/GRU over the last 5 box deltas (DiffMOT HMINet-like, n=5) of parameter count equal to the fly readout head if a learned motion branch is tested. Three-way comparison: appearance-only (base) / appearance + box-motion or R1 under the same gate (addition without fly) / appearance + FlyVis D under the same gate (addition with fly); a FlyVis result requires the third to beat the second.
bio_node_mapping: Box-trajectory motion (Kalman, velocity direction, learned box predictor) has no direct FlyVis node; the closest are T4/T5 direction-selective outputs integrated over the eye crop (a local motion-direction estimate) and the recurrent state of the FlyVis core (temporal integration). The motion-level gate resembles the insect strategy of switching between motion-based and feature-based pursuit (e.g., LC/LPLC lobula columnar neurons and STMD target detectors with facilitation) [uncertain: analogy, not supported by these sources]. Connectome data for T4/T5 and lobula LC types exist in FlyWire 783 (data/flywire/783 in the project); the current FlyVis model covers the optic lobe up to T4/T5, not LC/LPLC identity pathways.
novelty_overlap: Nearest prior: TOPIC (motion-level gating between motion and appearance matching) and DeconfuseTrack (appearance consulted only under positional ambiguity); our version would differ by gating a connectome-constrained motion-energy readout (FlyVis T4/T5) on top of a strong frozen appearance base for per-region identity, not choosing between box motion and ReID.
candidate_node_change: Readout node of FlyVis (state + readout): add a regime-gated identity readout - the FlyVis identity score is consulted only when a training-free ambiguity scalar (appearance top-2 margin from MASA, TOPIC-style motion level of the track, crowding of the eye crop) exceeds a threshold fixed on calibration videos; outside the gate the decision is appearance-only. Why it addresses a FlyVis problem: our fly evidence may be informative only in ambiguity subsets and diluted (or slightly harmful) elsewhere; the gate makes the fly readout's contribution measurable and prevents it from damaging the strong base (the DanceTrack/DeepSORT lesson). Equal controls under the identical gate and same boosting capacity: appearance only; appearance + stock C; appearance + eye input R1; appearance + box-motion (Kalman distance + velocity-direction cosine); appearance + within-query permuted fly rows. Condition to proceed to GPU (new FlyVis maps or core fine-tuning on identity): the CPU precheck shows (a) the perfect-identity ceiling is concentrated in an identifiable stratum, (b) inside that stratum FlyVis D is right where appearance is wrong more often than box-motion and R1 with a positive lower CI bound, and (c) the gated combination's train26 upper bound can still reach the +2 pp criterion. Otherwise record that the readout gate did not help and that the node of failure is the information content of FlyVis features, not the fusion.
strongest_objection: These sources are about the opposite regime: their objects look alike (dancers, bees, uniformed players) so appearance is weak and box motion is the strong cue; on BDD100K MASA appearance is already highly discriminative (same-track cosine 0.955 vs different 0.103, appearance AUC 0.965 on train26), the regime where DeconfuseTrack's pure motion module adds +0.1 HOTA and appearance-heavy bases gain nothing. Moreover the useful motion in these papers is box-trajectory motion that ByteTrack's Kalman already uses; FlyVis' T4/T5 signal inside a crop is a different and noisier quantity, and any gain obtained by gating may be reproduced by the trivial velocity-direction cue - which would make it a tracker improvement, not a FlyVis result. No source covers darkness/glare or driving data, and none reports variance, so the size of gating gains (+1.3..+2.0 HOTA in TOPIC) is single-run evidence.
cost_and_hardware: Steps 1-4 of the precheck: CPU only, on saved train26/fit104 features and tracker logs; hours of analyst time, minutes of compute (boosting refits per stratum with nested folds may take tens of minutes). Box-motion controls need only tracker states already saved [uncertain: whether last-k velocities are stored per query or must be recomputed from saved tracks on CPU]. New FlyVis activity maps or core fine-tuning on identity would need the single 12 GB GPU and are justified only if the decision rule passes.
